  * ####  [ Fix base type expansion for assignability check ](/eclipse-cyclonedds/cyclonedds/commit/3eb6575da547777080d60c767070b26bb4aedd86 "Fix base type expansion for assignability check

A type T with a base B that itself has a base type A would end up with the wrong list of
members in the assignability check:

  struct A { a1, a2 };
  struct B : A { b1 };
  struct T : B { t1 };

would yield:

  expand\(T\)
    B has base type => expand\(B\)
      A has no base type
      prepend fields of A to B'
      B' = { a1, a2, b1 }
    prepend fields of B \(not B'!\)
    T' = { b1, a1, a2, b1 }

This simplifies the code by always duplication the top-level type and then appending
members of derived types.

  * ####  [ Add ENABLE_TYPELIB build option ](/eclipse-cyclonedds/cyclonedds/commit/a4e00a7644fda7eda6eab9210d35e159ef2a8e29 "Add ENABLE_TYPELIB build option

This adds the ENABLE_TYPELIB build option \(default is ON\) that controls
including the type library \(which stores the type meta-data for types
used in local entities and in discovered proxy entities\). The
ENABLE_TYPELIB also controls the availability of the type-builder \(to
construct the type meta-data used by the serialized, e.g. used from the
Python API\) and the dynamic type API.

Most of the functionality that can be disabled/enabled with this option
was previously controlled by the ENABLE_TYPE_DISCOVERY build option.
That option is also still available, but now only controls the inclusion

Fix base type expansion for assignability check. More information available below.

Fix base type expansion for assignability check

A type T with a base B that itself has a base type A would end up with the wrong list of
members in the assignability check:

  struct A { a1, a2 };
  struct B : A { b1 };
  struct T : B { t1 };

would yield:

  expand(T)
    B has base type => expand(B)
      A has no base type
      prepend fields of A to B'
      B' = { a1, a2, b1 }
    prepend fields of B (not B'!)
    T' = { b1, a1, a2, b1 }

This simplifies the code by always duplication the top-level type and then appending
members of derived types.

type assignability (7.2.4.4) defines when T2 is assignability to T1, so T1 is the reader
type and T2 the writer type. In the section on type consistency (7.6.3.4), it discusses
what it means when T2 widens T1, which for the purposes of assignability really means the
case where T2 is the reader type and T1 the writer type.

Unfortunately, this made its way into the implementation and the test. It can also cause
an out-of-bounds read in the assignability check.

name.value: Fix base type expansion for assignability check

value.value: Fix base type expansion for assignability check

Fix base type expansion for assignability check

A type T with a base B that itself has a base type A would end up with the wrong list of
members in the assignability check:

  struct A { a1, a2 };
  struct B : A { b1 };
  struct T : B { t1 };

would yield:

  expand(T)
    B has base type => expand(B)
      A has no base type
      prepend fields of A to B'
      B' = { a1, a2, b1 }
    prepend fields of B (not B'!)
    T' = { b1, a1, a2, b1 }

This simplifies the code by always duplication the top-level type and then appending
members of derived types.

Signed-off-by: Erik Boasson <eb@ilities.com>

name.value: Allow empty structs in type validator

value.value: Allow empty structs in type validator

Allow empty structs in type validator

This allows empty structs in the type validator. Structs can
be defined in IDL with any number of members, including 0
(which is also used in the XTypes Type Object data types).
The IDL compiler C backend handles empty struct correctly, by
not creating a C struct for the type, because C does not allow
empty structs. But the type validator was incorrectly rejecting
type meta-data for an empty struct, which is changed in this PR.

Empty unions are still not allowed in the validator, because
there seems to be little practical value in supporting them
(however the spec is not clear at this point).

Add ENABLE_TYPELIB build option

This adds the ENABLE_TYPELIB build option (default is ON) that controls
including the type library (which stores the type meta-data for types
used in local entities and in discovered proxy entities). The
ENABLE_TYPELIB also controls the availability of the type-builder (to
construct the type meta-data used by the serialized, e.g. used from the
Python API) and the dynamic type API.

Most of the functionality that can be disabled/enabled with this option
was previously controlled by the ENABLE_TYPE_DISCOVERY build option.
That option is also still available, but now only controls the inclusion
of the type lookup functionality (that allows resolving type meta-data for
types from discovery endpoints or topics).
